key_insight: ImmunoStruct integrates molecular sequence, 3D structure, and biochemical features into a single multimodal deep learning model to predict immunogenicity with interpretable outputs, enabling hypothesis-driven molecular design.
problem_solved: Predicting immunogenicity is challenging because it depends on complex, interacting sequence, structural, and biochemical signals that single-modality models miss and are often uninterpretable for downstream experimental design.
method: Multimodal architecture that fuses sequence embeddings, 3D structural representations, and computed biochemical descriptors into a joint latent space.
Supervised training on curated experimental immunogenicity datasets with attention/saliency modules to provide per-residue and per-feature interpretability.
Benchmarking against unimodal baselines and providing case studies mapping model attributions onto molecular structures for hypothesis generation.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, ImmunoStruct demonstrates how multimodal fusion plus interpretability can improve predictive accuracy and actionable insight for bio-molecular design, accelerating vaccine and therapeutic discovery pipelines.
visual_elements: Schematic diagram of the multimodal pipeline: sequence, structure, and biochemical inputs → fusion model → immunogenicity score
Performance bar/curve comparing ImmunoStruct vs unimodal baselines (ROC/PR or AUC gains)
Attention/saliency heatmap overlaid on a 3D molecular structure to show interpretable hotspot predictions
Example case study panel: input molecule → predicted score → experimental validation highlight
paper_title: ImmunoStruct enables multimodal deep learning for immunogenicity prediction
paper_authors: Kevin Bijan Givechian, João Felipe Rocha, Chen Liu, Edward Yang, Sidharth Tyagi
